items.summary: President of India, acting through the Ministry of Finance has sold off 6.5% stake in Life Insurance Corporation of India (“ LIC ”), by way of an offer for sale through the stock exchange mechanism. Dentons Link Legal advised the President of India (Government) on this Offer for Sale. The transaction team consisted of Milind Jha (Partner), Aditya Bhardwaj (Associate Partner) and Shailender Sharma (Principal Associate). Milind Jha Trilegal represented the broker syndicate comprising Goldman Sachs, BNP Paribas, Motilal Oswal and IIFL Capital. The transaction was led by Richa Choudhary (Partner) and Maitreya Rajurkar (Partner), with support from Sanya Chaudhari (Senior Associate) and Naman Shah (Associate). Richa Choudhary, Maitreya Rajurkar Sidley Austin and FBT Gibbons also advised on this transaction. This monetisation exercise also enabled the Government of India to achieve approximately two-thirds of its budget estimate for miscellaneous receipts for Fiscal 2027. items.title: Spreading hatred: UP opposes Rahul Gandhi plea before Supreme Court in Savarkar remarks case
items.summary: Uttar Pradesh government has opposed Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi's petition in Supreme Court for quashing the summons issued to him by a Magistrate for making remarks against Hindutva idealogue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. The government has claimed that there was a "deliberate spreading of hatred through pre-planned actions" by Gandhi and thus, his appeal before the top court must be dismissed. " The Ld. Magistrate properly applied judicial mind to facts and evidence, determining a prima facie case under Section 153-A and 505 IPC ," the State said in reply to the notice issued to it by top court. The summons order was issued by a Lucknow Magistrate court on December 12, 2024. The Supreme Court had in April this year stayed the summons issued to Gandhi but taken strong exception to his remarks that Savarkar was a collaborator with the British who received pension from them. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Manmohan had then remarked that Gandhi's statements against the freedom fighter were irresponsible and that the Court will initiate suo motu action if he makes similar statements.
